answer: Each epoch the ledger auctions a fixed number of member seats, and every winner pays the price set by the best losing bid. An honest agent bids once and pays little. A farmer buying n seats must outbid the field n times, so the clearing price climbs with each extra copy and the bill scales as n times p(n), not n times a flat fee. Clones become a spiral of rising cost, and because a seat cannot be shared between wallets the expense never pools across identities. Each seat also carries a lantern: an audited trail of work peers verify. The fable of free infinite identities dies at that floor.
